#updated research question:
#Do major US airlines differ significantly in their joint departure and arrival delays. If so, what are the possible drivers of the delays

#POSSIBLE PREDICTORS: 
#busyness(no of flights departing from each airport)
#origin state 
#destination state 
#distance traveled
#scheduled departure time
#season - does it affect time blocks?


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Upload Data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(car)
library(broom)

flights <- read_csv("./flights_sample.csv")

# Inspect the data
dim(flights)
names(flights)
glimpse(flights)

```

Data Cleaning: Remove missing values
```{r}
flights_clean <- flights %>%
  filter(
    cancelled == 0,
    diverted == 0,
    !is.na(dep_delay),
    !is.na(arr_delay)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    FL_DATE = as.Date(flight_date),

    MONTH = month(flight_date),

    DAY_OF_WEEK = wday(flight_date, label = TRUE),

    DEP_PERIOD = case_when(
      dep_time < 600 ~ "Early Morning",
      dep_time < 1200 ~ "Morning",
      dep_time < 1800 ~ "Afternoon",
      TRUE ~ "Evening"
    ),

    DELAY_RECOVERY = dep_delay - arr_delay
  )

dim(flights_clean)
# Removed about 10,000 rows and 5 columns
#Excludes cancelled and diverted flights
#Does not replace missing values with 0
```

Exploratory Analysis
```{r}
# Departure vs. arrival delay
ggplot(flights_clean,
       aes(x = dep_delay, y = arr_delay)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Departure and Arrival Delays",
    x = "Departure Delay (minutes)",
    y = "Arrival Delay (minutes)"
  )

# Average delays by airline
flights_clean %>%
  group_by(airline) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_dep = mean(dep_delay),
    mean_arr = mean(arr_delay)
  )

```

Correlation Matrices among variables
```{r}
library(corrplot)
names(flights_clean)

numeric_data <- flights_clean %>%
  select(
    dep_delay,
    arr_delay,
    year,
    distance,
    air_time,
    taxi_out,
    taxi_in
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data)

corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black")

# Pearson correlation
cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs",
    method = "pearson")

```
Strong correlations between arrival delay and departure delay, as well as
airtime and distance. 
I also believe there may be Simpson's Paradox at play, where the variables
may show a higher correlation when we group by Airline.

## Create a subset of the dataset with the predictors of interest and create
##some metrics 

Upload data and examine dataset
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)

# Load dataset
flights <- read_csv("./flights_sample.csv") %>%
  clean_names()

# Examine dataset
dim(flights)
names(flights)
glimpse(flights)

#investigating missingness
naniar::miss_var_summary(flights) #results suggest that missingness may be systematic rather than random

flights |>
  count(cancelled, is.na(cancellation_reason))
#all non-cancelled flights have missing cancellation reasons
#there are no cancelled flights with missing cancellation reasons
#we can keep in case we want to investigate cancellation reasons

flights |>
  count(arr_del15, missing_carrier_delay = is.na(carrier_delay))
#we actually have missing arrival-delay indicators and also have missing carrier delay values

delay_vars <- c(
  "carrier_delay",
  "weather_delay",
  "nas_delay",
  "security_delay",
  "late_aircraft_delay"
)

flights %>%
  group_by(arr_del15) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(delay_vars),
      ~ sum(is.na(.x))
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
#missing values were only recorded for flights that arrived at least 15 mins late
#flights that do not meet this threshold have missing vlaues for all 5 variables

flights %>%
  count(
    cancelled,
    diverted,
    missing_arr_delay = is.na(arr_delay)
  )
#all cancelled and diverted flights have missing arrival delays.
#the 2.07% missingness in arrival delay is entirely explained by cancellations and diversions

# Number and percentage of missing values per variable
missing_summary <- flights %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_missing = round(missing / nrow(flights_top5) * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(percent_missing))

missing_summary

```

Limit data to the top five airlines
```{r}

# Rank airlines by number of flights
top5_airlines <- flights %>%
  count(airline, airline_code, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)

top5_airlines

# Visualize flight counts
ggplot(top5_airlines,
       aes(x = reorder(airline, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top Five Airlines by Number of Flights",
    x = "Airline",
    y = "Number of Flights"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

Calculate airport busyness metric
```{r}

total_flights <- nrow(flights)

# Origin airport activity
origin_busy <- flights %>%
  count(origin, name = "origin_flight_count") %>%
  mutate(
    origin_busyness = origin_flight_count / total_flights
  )

# Destination airport activity
dest_busy <- flights %>%
  count(dest, name = "dest_flight_count") %>%
  mutate(
    dest_busyness = dest_flight_count / total_flights
  )

# Join airport activity measures to flight data
flights <- flights %>%
  left_join(origin_busy, by = "origin") %>%
  left_join(dest_busy, by = "dest")

```

Create season metric based on departure date, and blocks of time for
scheduled departure time
```{r}

flights <- flights %>%
  mutate(
    flight_date = as.Date(flight_date),

    # Season
    month = month(flight_date),

    season = case_when(
      month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
      month %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Spring",
      month %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Summer",
      month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    season = factor(
      season,
      levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
    ),

    # Extract scheduled departure hour
    dep_hour = floor(sched_dep_time / 100),

    # Departure period
    dep_period = case_when(
      dep_hour >= 0 & dep_hour < 8 ~ "Early Morning",
      dep_hour >= 6 & dep_hour < 12 ~ "Morning",
      dep_hour >= 12 & dep_hour < 18 ~ "Afternoon",
      dep_hour >= 18 & dep_hour < 24 ~ "Evening",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    dep_period = factor(
      dep_period,
      levels = c(
        "Early Morning",
        "Morning",
        "Afternoon",
        "Evening"
      )
    )
  )

```

Add origin and destination states
```{r}

flights_top5 <- flights %>%
  semi_join(
    top5_airlines,
    by = c("airline", "airline_code")
  )

# Check final dataset
dim(flights_top5)
glimpse(flights_top5)

# Verify airline counts
flights_top5 %>%
  count(airline, sort = TRUE)

```

Validate final dataset
```{r}

# Check missing values
missing_summary <- flights_top5 %>%
  summarise(across(everything(),
                   ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_count"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

missing_summary

# Check season distribution
flights_top5 %>%
  count(season)

# Check departure period distribution
flights_top5 %>%
  count(dep_period)

# Check airport busyness
summary(flights_top5$origin_busyness)
summary(flights_top5$dest_busyness)

# Check date range
range(flights_top5$flight_date, na.rm = TRUE)

# Check cancellations and diversions
flights_top5 %>%
  summarise(
    cancellation_rate = mean(cancelled == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    diversion_rate = mean(diverted == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#Check airlines is top 5 only
flights_top5 %>%
  count(airline)

#Final Dataset:
flights_top5

```
